--- Page 1 ---
Daniel legte den Umschlag mitten auf den Gartentisch — einen großen, knallgelben Umschlag mit einem roten Fragezeichen drauf. „Irgendwo im Garten und im Haus", sagte er, „liegt ein Schatz versteckt. Dieser Brief erklärt euch, wo ihr anfangen sollt." Er zog eine kleine Taschenlampe aus der Tasche und legte sie neben den Umschlag. „Die könnt ihr brauchen."

Emma griff blitzschnell zu. Noah griff genauso schnell zu. Einen Moment lang hielten beide den Umschlag fest.

„Ich lese vor!", rief Emma.
„Ich bin älter!", sagte Noah.

Sie rissen ihn gleichzeitig auf. Der erste Zettel flatterte auf den Tisch: *Sucht dort, wo die Tomaten rot werden.* Emma war bereits auf den Beinen, bevor Noah den Satz zu Ende gelesen hatte. Hinter ihnen stieß Daniel seinen Kaffeebecher um.

--- Page 2 ---
Das Tomatenbeet lag am Rand des Gartens, dicht neben dem Komposthaufen. Emma kniete sich hin und wühlte zwischen den großen grünen Blättern. „Nichts!", rief sie. Sie wühlte noch tiefer. „Gar nichts!"

Noah stand mit verschränkten Armen daneben. „Du hast falsch geguckt. Der Zettel sagt *wo die Tomaten rot werden* — die hier sind noch grün." Er schnaufte. „Wegen dir haben wir jetzt Zeit verloren."

Sarah hob die Hand. Sie hatte die ganze Zeit an der Rosenhecke gestanden. „Darf ich mal sehen?" Sie nahm den Zettel, las ihn langsam und hob eine Augenbraue. „Wo werden Tomaten rot?" Sie wartete.

Emma öffnete den Mund. Schloss ihn wieder. „In der Küche", sagte sie leise. „Im Obstkorb."

--- Page 3 ---
Der Zettel, den sie in der Küche fanden, zeigte einen gezeichneten Schlüssel und die Worte: *Tief unten, im Dunkel, wartet dein Schatz.*

Noah rannte zur Kellertür. Er riss sie auf. Eine schmale Holztreppe führte hinunter in die Schwärze.

Emma blieb an der Türschwelle stehen. Da unten war kein Licht. Ihr Herz klopfte schnell.

„Kommst du?", rief Noah von unten. Seine Stimme klang weit weg.

Emma zog die kleine Taschenlampe aus der Jackentasche. Sie drückte den Knopf. Ein Lichtstrahl fiel die Treppe hinab. Dann machte sie einen Schritt in die Dunkelheit.

--- Page 4 ---
Unten, im Schein der Taschenlampe, stand eine alte Holzkiste mit einem schweren Eisenriegel.

„Ich kriege ihn nicht auf!", sagte Noah. Er drückte mit beiden Daumen dagegen. Nichts bewegte sich.

Emma kniete sich neben ihn. „Zusammen." Sie legte ihre Hände neben seine. Auf drei drückten sie gemeinsam — und der Riegel sprang auf mit einem lauten *Klack*.

Kurze Zeit später saßen alle im Sonnenschein um den Gartentisch. Die Kiste stand in der Mitte. Darin lagen zwei hübsch eingepackte Päckchen. Emma schob das eine zu Noah hinüber. „Das ist bestimmt deins."

Hans hob sein Glas Limonade. „Auf den besten Schatz von allen", sagte er.

Sarah lächelte. Sie hatte schon gewusst, wie es enden würde.

A tipped coffee mug, a clue note, and a small silver flashlight sit on the table between them. Daniel stands behind the table reaching toward the fallen mug in warm garden sunlight.

Generate a SINGLE illustration filling the ENTIRE canvas edge-to-edge. No borders, no frames, no margins, no white edges. No split screen, no panels, no grid, no collage. The artwork must extend to all four edges. All surfaces in the scene — walls, shutters, vehicles, garments, paper, screens, pole-mounted boards, shopfronts — render free of written characters, letters, numbers, or symbols, unless the scene description explicitly names the text to show. Character names from the prompt (e.g. labels like `[Noah]`, `[Emma]`) are reference identifiers only — never paint them onto clothing, signs, banners, captions, name tags, or any surface in the scene.

When the FIRST reference photo shows a real location (architecture, landscape, no characters in it), render the scene IN that location — copy its setting, architecture, geography, and lighting. All OTHER reference photos define each character's IDENTITY only — face, hair, skin tone, build, and clothing — never their pose, framing, or composition. Characters' positions, actions, body direction, and size come entirely from the scene description and the COMPOSITION rules below.

**Clothing for each named character (must match the attached labeled portrait):**
- Emma: light pink long-sleeve shirt, dark blue jeans, white velcro sneakers, small stud earrings
- Noah: green and white striped short-sleeve shirt, grey jogger trousers, blue and white trainers
- Daniel: navy blue casual button-up shirt with sleeves rolled to elbows, khaki trousers, brown leather loafers

**HEIGHT ORDER (shortest to tallest):** Emma (shortest) -> Noah (taller) -> Daniel (noticeably taller)

Emma — a preschooler-looks girl with brown wavy ear-length hair in a ponytail with a side part on the right, brown eyes, soft rounded features, freckles, and small stud earrings — stands at the near edge of a wooden garden table in the foreground, both hands gripping a large bright-yellow envelope with a red question mark on it, leaning forward with wide eyes facing Noah across the table. Noah — a kindergartner-looks boy with blonde wavy ear-length hair with bangs at his eyebrows, blue eyes, and soft rounded features — stands at the opposite side of the table in the midground, also gripping the same yellow envelope with both hands, facing Emma with brows pulled together. Between them on the rough wooden table surface sit a white ceramic coffee mug tipped on its side with a small dark spill spreading outward, a folded white paper clue note half unrolled, and a small palm-sized silver flashlight lying flat. In the background, Daniel — an adult man with dark brown wavy short hair, a short beard and mustache, brown eyes, and adult proportions — stands behind the table, one hand reaching toward the tipped mug, body facing the table. The garden setting surrounds them: sunny green lawn, a low wooden fence along the back edge, flowering shrubs in soft focus behind Daniel. Warm midday sunlight falls from above, casting short shadows on the tabletop. Wide shot, lively atmosphere.

**COMPOSITION:**
- Characters must INTERACT with the scene — facing and engaging with objects, landmarks, or each other. NOT standing in front of a backdrop looking at the viewer.
- Characters face TOWARD what they interact with. Eyes look at objects or other characters, NOT at the camera.
- If a character is INTERACTING with something in the BACKGROUND (running toward the castle, looking up at the tower, walking toward the bridge), they face that direction — back or side to the camera. If the character's interaction target is in foreground or midground, they face that target instead, with face visible to the reader.
- Each character must be DOING something specific (reaching, looking at, holding, walking toward). No static posing.
- **DEPTH — read each character's position label and honour it:** "foreground" characters fill roughly the lower half of the frame, large, with feet on the ground. "midground" characters occupy the MIDDLE BAND — heads do NOT reach the top edge, feet do NOT reach the bottom edge. "background" characters are small, distant, far behind. Foreground larger than midground larger than background.
- **KEEP THE FOREGROUND (LOWER STRIP) EMPTY** unless a character is explicitly labelled "foreground". When all characters are midground or background the bottom portion shows only the natural ground of this scene (cobblestones, floor, water, grass, sand, snow). When any character IS labelled foreground, that character's body and feet belong in this strip.

**ERFORDERLICHE OBJEKTE IN DIESER SZENE (MÜSSEN im Bild erscheinen):**
* **Garten mit Holztisch** (location): outdoor, private garden. Colors: green lawn, warm brown wooden table, soft cream fence boards. rough-hewn rectangular wooden garden table at center, four wooden chairs, low cream-painted wooden fence along back edge, rose hedge to one side, lawn grass throughout. Signature: the rough wooden garden table with visible grain and natural knots
* **Gelber Umschlag mit Fragezeichen** (object): A large A5-sized bright yellow paper envelope with a bold red question mark hand-drawn on the front face in thick marker; the flap is torn open at the top, white inner paper visible; slightly crumpled from two sets of small hands gripping it
* **Hinweiszettel** (object): A palm-sized white paper note, folded once horizontally, with a single line of text written in neat black handwriting; slightly creased along the fold line; plain white paper with no decorative border

**ART STYLE:** A traditional watercolor painting in the style of Inga Moore. Realistic human proportions across all ages — children look like children, teenagers look visibly older than children, adults look like adults. Textured paper with pencil underpainting, delicate color washes with wet-on-wet technique, soft paint edges, visible artistic brushstrokes, and luminous flowing colors. Characters are fully opaque — never see-through, never fading into the background. Warm but not overly vibrant color palette with visible paper texture throughout. Faces: watercolor wash rendering with visible brushstroke texture, age-appropriate features with defined bone structure. Eyes naturally sized. Never sharp or digitally rendered.

- Emma: Emma grips the left side of the yellow envelope, Noah grips the right side, both pulling toward themselves across the table
- Noah: Emma grips the left side of the yellow envelope, Noah grips the right side, both pulling toward themselves across the table
- Daniel: reaches toward the tipped mug on the table surface

  * Do NOT make the box too narrow — include the full head width

  * The face_box should be roughly square for a front-facing figure
- body_box: bounding box around the FULL FIGURE (or as much as visible)
- If the head is not visible (back view, non-human creature), set face_box to null

- Report "found": true/false for each expected object
- If found, include body_box bounding box and position

- Hinweiszettel



COORDINATE SYSTEM:
- Values are 0-1000 (Gemini native format)
- Origin is top-left corner
- Format: [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max]

FIGURE COUNT LIMIT:
- Return AT MOST 10 figures total. If the scene has a crowd in the background, do NOT enumerate each crowd member as a separate figure — the crowd is backdrop, not a list.
- Only include a figure if its face OR body occupies at least ~5% of the frame width or height. Tiny silhouettes in the distance are backdrop, skip them.
- If you cannot distinguish between several figures (e.g. multiple blurred robes in the background), return ONE figure representing the group and set `name: "UNKNOWN"`, `label: "background crowd"` — never duplicate the same label across many entries.

FOR EACH FIGURE (up to 10, including partially visible ones near the edges of main subjects):
- If you can identify it as an expected character, set "name" to the character name (EXACTLY as listed above)
- Use CLOTHING + POSITION to distinguish figures (two figures with similar build are distinguished by what they wear and where they stand)
- If not identifiable as any expected character, set "name" to "UNKNOWN"

- Report "found": true/false for each expected object

- DO NOT list everything the figure is wearing. DO NOT describe actions. DO NOT describe expressions.

Emma — a preschooler-looks girl with brown wavy hair cut to ear-length and gathered into a small ponytail, side-parted on the right, brown eyes, freckles across her nose and cheeks, and small stud earrings, wearing her standard outfit — sits at the rough-hewn wooden garden table in the midground, leaning forward over the open wooden chest that sits on the table surface between her and Noah, her right hand reaching down into the chest toward two small parcels wrapped in red and blue paper. Beside Emma on her right sits Noah — a kindergartner-looks boy with blonde wavy ear-length hair and bangs falling to his eyebrows, blue eyes, soft rounded features, wearing his standard outfit — both hands resting on the rim of the chest, his gaze directed down at the parcels inside, body leaning in toward the chest. To Noah's right at the same table sits Hans — an elderly man with white straight short combed hair, a prominent white mustache, brown eyes, and a rounded jawline, wearing his standard outfit — holding a fist-sized glass of lemonade at chest height, his body facing Emma and Noah and his eyes on them. To Emma's left at the table sits Sarah — an adult woman with blonde straight chin-length hair combed with a side part on the left, blue eyes, and rectangular dark-framed glasses, wearing her standard outfit — body facing the open chest, her gaze directed down at the chest on the table, not at the camera. Daniel — an adult man with dark brown wavy short hair, a short beard and mustache, brown eyes, wearing his standard outfit — stands near the garden fence in the background, body facing the table and the seated group, a small but clearly forward-facing figure roughly one-quarter the height of the foreground characters. Warm late-afternoon sunlight casts long shadows across the tabletop and lawn. Wide shot, garden setting with the rough-grained wooden table at center and the low cream-painted fence behind the group.

Character names from the prompt (e.g. labels like `[Noah]`, `[Emma]`) are reference identifiers only — never paint them onto clothing, signs, banners, captions, name tags, or any surface in the scene.

When the FIRST reference photo shows a real location (architecture, landscape, no characters in it), render the scene IN that location — copy its setting, architecture, geography, and lighting. All OTHER reference photos define each character's IDENTITY only — face, hair, skin tone, build, and clothing — never their pose, framing, or composition. Characters' positions, actions, body direction, and size come entirely from the scene description and the COMPOSITION rules below.

**HEIGHT ORDER (shortest to tallest):** Emma (shortest) -> Noah (taller) -> Sarah (noticeably taller) -> Hans (slightly taller) -> Daniel (similar height)

Emma — a preschooler-looks girl with brown wavy hair cut to ear-length and gathered into a small ponytail, side-parted on the right, brown eyes, freckles across her nose and cheeks, and small stud earrings, wearing her standard outfit — sits at the rough-hewn wooden garden table in the midground, leaning forward over the open wooden chest that sits on the table surface between her and Noah, her right hand reaching down into the chest toward two small parcels wrapped in red and blue paper. Beside Emma on her right sits Noah — a kindergartner-looks boy with blonde wavy ear-length hair and bangs falling to his eyebrows, blue eyes, soft rounded features, wearing his standard outfit — both hands resting on the rim of the chest, his gaze directed down at the parcels inside, body leaning in toward the chest. To Noah's right at the same table sits Hans — an elderly man with white straight short combed hair, a prominent white mustache, brown eyes, and a rounded jawline, wearing his standard outfit — holding a fist-sized glass of lemonade at chest height, his body facing Emma and Noah and his eyes on them. To Emma's left at the table sits Sarah — an adult woman with blonde straight chin-length hair combed with a side part on the left, blue eyes, and rectangular dark-framed glasses, wearing her standard outfit — body facing the open chest, her gaze directed down at the chest on the table, not at the camera. Daniel — an adult man with dark brown wavy short hair, a short beard and mustache, brown eyes, wearing his standard outfit — stands near the garden fence in the background, body facing the table and the seated group, a small but clearly forward-facing figure roughly one-quarter the height of the foreground characters. Warm late-afternoon sunlight casts long shadows across the tabletop and lawn. Wide shot, garden setting with the rough-grained wooden table at center and the low cream-painted fence behind the group.

**COMPOSITION:**
- Characters must INTERACT with the scene — facing and engaging with objects, landmarks, or each other. NOT standing in front of a backdrop looking at the viewer.
- Characters face TOWARD what they interact with. Eyes look at objects or other characters, NOT at the camera.
- If a character is INTERACTING with something in the BACKGROUND (running toward the castle, looking up at the tower, walking toward the bridge), they face that direction — back or side to the camera. If the character's interaction target is in foreground or midground, they face that target instead, with face visible to the reader.
- Each character must be DOING something specific (reaching, looking at, holding, walking toward). No static posing.
- **DEPTH — read each character's position label and honour it:** "foreground" characters fill roughly the lower half of the frame, large, with feet on the ground. "midground" characters occupy the MIDDLE BAND — heads do NOT reach the top edge, feet do NOT reach the bottom edge. "background" characters are small, distant, far behind. Foreground larger than midground larger than background.
- **KEEP THE FOREGROUND (LOWER STRIP) EMPTY** unless a character is explicitly labelled "foreground". When all characters are midground or background the bottom portion shows only the natural ground of this scene (cobblestones, floor, water, grass, sand, snow). When any character IS labelled foreground, that character's body and feet belong in this strip.

Signature: the rough wooden garden table with visible grain and natural knots

imageVersionsMeta.description:
Emma — a preschooler-looks girl with brown wavy ear-length hair pulled back in a short ponytail with a side part, brown eyes, freckles, and small stud earrings, wearing her standard outfit — sits at the rough-hewn rectangular wooden garden table in the midground, leaning forward with one arm extended and her hand reaching down into the open wooden chest that sits on the table surface between her and Noah. Noah — a kindergartner-looks boy with blonde wavy ear-length hair with bangs at his eyebrows, blue eyes, and soft rounded features, wearing his standard outfit — sits beside Emma at the same table, both hands resting on the rim of the open chest, his gaze fixed on the two small parcels wrapped in red and blue paper inside the chest. Hans — an elderly man with white straight short combed hair, a prominent white mustache, brown eyes, and a rounded jawline, wearing his standard outfit — sits at the table to Noah's side, holding a fist-sized glass of clear yellow lemonade at chest height, facing Emma and Noah across the table. Sarah — an adult woman with straight blonde chin-length hair combed with a side part, blue eyes, and rectangular dark-framed glasses on her face, wearing her standard outfit — sits at the table on Emma's other side, leaning slightly forward, facing the open chest on the table surface; her hands rest on the table edge. Daniel — an adult man with dark brown wavy short hair, a short beard and mustache, and brown eyes, wearing his standard outfit — stands near the low cream-painted wooden garden fence in the background, a small figure behind the seated group, facing the table. The wooden chest sits squarely on the table's rough grain surface, its lid open and iron hinges visible, the two wrapped parcels inside. Warm late-afternoon sunlight falls across the tabletop and casts long shadows along the wood grain. Wide shot.

The artwork must extend to all four edges. Character names from the prompt (e.g. labels like `[Noah]`, `[Emma]`) are reference identifiers only — never paint them onto clothing, signs, banners, captions, name tags, or any surface in the scene.

When the FIRST reference photo shows a real location (architecture, landscape, no characters in it), render the scene IN that location — copy its setting, architecture, geography, and lighting. All OTHER reference photos define each character's IDENTITY only — face, hair, skin tone, build, and clothing — never their pose, framing, or composition. **COMPOSITION:**
- Characters must INTERACT with the scene — facing and engaging with objects, landmarks, or each other. NOT standing in front of a backdrop looking at the viewer.
- Characters face TOWARD what they interact with. Eyes look at objects or other characters, NOT at the camera.
- If a character is INTERACTING with something in the BACKGROUND (running toward the castle, looking up at the tower, walking toward the bridge), they face that direction — back or side to the camera. - Each character must be DOING something specific (reaching, looking at, holding, walking toward). No static posing.
- **DEPTH — read each character's position label and honour it:** "foreground" characters fill roughly the lower half of the frame, large, with feet on the ground. "midground" characters occupy the MIDDLE BAND — heads do NOT reach the top edge, feet do NOT reach the bottom edge. "background" characters are small, distant, far behind. Foreground larger than midground larger than background.
- **KEEP THE FOREGROUND (LOWER STRIP) EMPTY** unless a character is explicitly labelled "foreground".    Expected position: right side of garden table, midground

EXPECTED OBJECTS (check if present):
- Garten mit Holztisch
- Holzkiste mit Eisenriegel



COORDINATE SYSTEM:
- Values are 0-1000 (Gemini native format)
- Origin is top-left corner
- Format: [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max]

FIGURE COUNT LIMIT:
- Return AT MOST 10 figures total. If the scene has a crowd in the background, do NOT enumerate each crowd member as a separate figure — the crowd is backdrop, not a list.
- Only include a figure if its face OR body occupies at least ~5% of the frame width or height. Tiny silhouettes in the distance are backdrop, skip them.
- If you cannot distinguish between several figures (e.g. multiple blurred robes in the background), return ONE figure representing the group and set `name: "UNKNOWN"`, `label: "background crowd"` — never duplicate the same label across many entries.

FOR EACH FIGURE (up to 10, including partially visible ones near the edges of main subjects):
- If you can identify it as an expected character, set "name" to the character name (EXACTLY as listed above)
- Use CLOTHING + POSITION to distinguish figures (two figures with similar build are distinguished by what they wear and where they stand)
- If not identifiable as any expected character, set "name" to "UNKNOWN"
- Include "confidence": "high", "medium", or "low" for identification certainty
- face_box: bounding box around the head region.
  Include the top of the head and the bottom of the head outline, and the full width from side to side.

  * Do NOT cut off the top of the head — include the full head outline
  * Do NOT cut off the bottom of the head outline
  * Do NOT make the box too narrow — include the full head width
  * When in doubt, make the face_box LARGER rather than smaller
  * The face_box should be roughly square for a front-facing figure
- body_box: bounding box around the FULL FIGURE (or as much as visible)
- If the head is not visible (back view, non-human creature), set face_box to null

FOR EXPECTED OBJECTS:
- Report "found": true/false for each expected object
- If found, include body_box bounding box and position

LABEL LENGTH RULE (non-negotiable):
- Every `label` field MUST be ≤ 10 words.
- Name ONE defining clothing item + ONE distinguishing feature. Example: "boy in blue hoodie with backpack".
- DO NOT list everything the figure is wearing. DO NOT describe actions. DO NOT describe expressions.

frontCover.prompt:
Generate a SINGLE illustration filling the ENTIRE canvas edge-to-edge. No borders, no frames, no margins, no white edges. No split screen, no panels, no grid, no collage. The artwork must extend to all four edges. All surfaces in the scene — walls, shutters, vehicles, garments, paper, screens, pole-mounted boards, shopfronts — render free of written characters, letters, numbers, or symbols, unless the scene description explicitly names the text to show.

Create a front cover illustration for a children's book.

**SCENE:**
Curious excitement and shared discovery. A wide group portrait set before Garten mit Holztisch. Emma, 5-year-old female, stands in the left-center foreground, holds the Gelber Umschlag mit Fragezeichen, eyes on the Holzkiste mit Eisenriegel. Noah, 7-year-old male, stands in the right-center foreground, holds the Holzkiste mit Eisenriegel, eyes on the Gelber Umschlag mit Fragezeichen.

**CHARACTER REFERENCE PHOTOS (one per character, labeled images attached below):** [Emma], [Noah]

**HEIGHT ORDER (shortest to tallest):** Emma (shortest) -> Noah (taller)

**ART STYLE:** A traditional watercolor painting in the style of Inga Moore. Realistic human proportions across all ages — children look like children, teenagers look visibly older than children, adults look like adults. Textured paper with pencil underpainting, delicate color washes with wet-on-wet technique, soft paint edges, visible artistic brushstrokes, and luminous flowing colors. Characters are fully opaque — never see-through, never fading into the background. Warm but not overly vibrant color palette with visible paper texture throughout. Faces: watercolor wash rendering with visible brushstroke texture, age-appropriate features with defined bone structure. Eyes naturally sized. Never sharp or digitally rendered.

**COMPOSITION GUIDELINES:**
- ALL MAIN CHARACTERS should be prominently featured and clearly recognizable
- Characters should be arranged in a balanced composition (side by side, or grouped naturally)
- Keep the composition simple and uncluttered
- Leave clear space at the TOP for the title text
- Each character has 2 hands. Show at most 2 items held per character — if more are mentioned, drop the rest.

**TEXT REQUIREMENT - CRITICAL:**
The image MUST include this exact title text: "Was Daniel vergessen hatte zu sagen"
- Position the title in the upper third of the image
- The letters have significant three-dimensional volume — they are physical objects in the scene, not flat text. They catch the scene's lighting and cast shadows like any other object would. Their color is not uniform but shaped by the light sources in the scene
- Use an artistic hand-crafted lettering style that fits the story's world — never standard computer fonts
- The title is the ONLY text that should appear in the image

**KEY STORY ELEMENTS:**
**Gelber Umschlag mit Fragezeichen** (artifact): A large A5-sized bright yellow paper envelope with a bold red question mark hand-drawn on the front face in thick marker; the flap is torn open at the top, white inner paper visible; slightly crumpled from two sets of small hands gripping it
**Hinweiszettel** (artifact): A palm-sized white paper note, folded once horizontally, with a single line of text written in neat black handwriting; slightly creased along the fold line; plain white paper with no decorative border
**Holzkiste mit Eisenriegel** (artifact): A forearm-length rectangular wooden chest with dark brown stained pine planks, iron corner brackets, and a heavy flat iron bar latch on the front face that slides horizontally through two iron loop brackets; the lid is hinged at the back with two visible iron hinges; inside, two small rectangular parcels wrapped in red and blue paper respectively

bboxDetection.rawPrompt:
Detect the 2d bounding boxes of all figures and objects in this illustrated image.

EXPECTED CHARACTERS (identify by name if found):
1. Emma - Emma is a preschooler little girl (Looks: preschooler), average build. Hair: brown, wavy, ear-length, ponytail, side part right, soft jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips, freckles, small stud earrings
2. Noah - Noah is a kindergartner little boy (Looks: kindergartner), average build. Hair: blonde, wavy, ear-length, bangs at eyebrows, soft jawline, neutral chin, straight nose with rounded tip, medium cheekbones, medium lips

(No expected objects provided)



COORDINATE SYSTEM:
- Values are 0-1000 (Gemini native format)
- Origin is top-left corner
- Format: [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max]

FIGURE COUNT LIMIT:
- Return AT MOST 10 figures total. If the scene has a crowd in the background, do NOT enumerate each crowd member as a separate figure — the crowd is backdrop, not a list.
- Only include a figure if its face OR body occupies at least ~5% of the frame width or height. Tiny silhouettes in the distance are backdrop, skip them.
- If you cannot distinguish between several figures (e.g. multiple blurred robes in the background), return ONE figure representing the group and set `name: "UNKNOWN"`, `label: "background crowd"` — never duplicate the same label across many entries.

FOR EACH FIGURE (up to 10, including partially visible ones near the edges of main subjects):
- If you can identify it as an expected character, set "name" to the character name (EXACTLY as listed above)
- Use CLOTHING + POSITION to distinguish figures (two figures with similar build are distinguished by what they wear and where they stand)
- If not identifiable as any expected character, set "name" to "UNKNOWN"
- Include "confidence": "high", "medium", or "low" for identification certainty
- face_box: bounding box around the head region.
  Include the top of the head and the bottom of the head outline, and the full width from side to side.
  Common mistakes to AVOID:
  * Do NOT cut off the top of the head — include the full head outline
  * Do NOT cut off the bottom of the head outline
  * Do NOT make the box too narrow — include the full head width
  * When in doubt, make the face_box LARGER rather than smaller
  * The face_box should be roughly square for a front-facing figure
- body_box: bounding box around the FULL FIGURE (or as much as visible)
- If the head is not visible (back view, non-human creature), set face_box to null

FOR EXPECTED OBJECTS:
- Report "found": true/false for each expected object
- If found, include body_box bounding box and position

LABEL LENGTH RULE (non-negotiable):
- Every `label` field MUST be ≤ 10 words.
- Name ONE defining clothing item + ONE distinguishing feature. Example: "boy in blue hoodie with backpack".
- DO NOT list everything the figure is wearing. DO NOT describe actions. DO NOT describe expressions.
- Long labels waste response tokens and cause the JSON to truncate before closing.

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "figures": [
    {
      "name": "CharacterName or UNKNOWN",
      "label": "≤10 words — one defining item + one distinguishing feature",

      "label": "visual description if found",
      "position": "left|center|right",
      "body_box": [y_min, x_min, y_max, x_max] or null
    }
  ]
}

sceneDescriptions.description:
Emma — a preschooler-looks girl with brown wavy ear-length hair in a ponytail with a side part on the right, brown eyes, soft rounded features, freckles, and small stud earrings — stands at the near edge of a wooden garden table in the foreground, both hands gripping a large bright-yellow envelope with a red question mark on it, leaning forward with wide eyes facing Noah across the table. Noah — a kindergartner-looks boy with blonde wavy ear-length hair with bangs at his eyebrows, blue eyes, and soft rounded features — stands at the opposite side of the table in the midground, also gripping the same yellow envelope with both hands, facing Emma with brows pulled together. Between them on the rough wooden table surface sit a white ceramic coffee mug tipped on its side with a small dark spill spreading outward, a folded white paper clue note half unrolled, and a small palm-sized silver flashlight lying flat. In the background, Daniel — an adult man with dark brown wavy short hair, a short beard and mustache, brown eyes, and adult proportions — stands behind the table, one hand reaching toward the tipped mug, body facing the table. The garden setting surrounds them: sunny green lawn, a low wooden fence along the back edge, flowering shrubs in soft focus behind Daniel. Warm midday sunlight falls from above, casting short shadows on the tabletop. Wide shot, lively atmosphere.

sceneDescriptions.description:
Emma — a preschooler-looks girl with brown wavy ear-length hair in a ponytail with a side part on the right, brown eyes, freckles, and small stud earrings — and Noah — a kindergartner-looks boy with blonde wavy ear-length hair with bangs at his eyebrows, blue eyes, soft rounded features — sit side by side at the wooden garden table in the midground, both leaning forward over the open wooden treasure chest between them on the table surface. Emma reaches one hand into the chest toward the two small wrapped parcels inside; Noah rests both hands on the chest's rim, gazing at the parcels. Hans — an elderly man with white straight short combed hair, a prominent white mustache, brown eyes, rounded jawline, and older adult proportions — sits at the table to Noah's right in the midground, holding a fist-sized glass of lemonade at chest height, facing Emma and Noah. Sarah — an adult woman with blonde straight chin-length hair combed with a side part on the left, blue eyes, and rectangular dark-framed glasses — sits at the table to Emma's left in the midground, facing the open chest. Daniel — an adult man with dark brown wavy short hair, a short beard and mustache, brown eyes, and adult proportions — stands near the garden fence in the background, facing the table. Warm late-afternoon sunlight casts long shadows across the tabletop. Wide shot, warm celebratory atmosphere.
